section_summary: This section follows the proposed salvage of the Japanese steamship Kowa Maru, wrecked near Balabac, and Philippine objections to unauthorized Japanese salvage activity. Correspondence addresses the vessel’s deteriorated condition, diplomatic permission, and whether foreign salvage vessels could operate in Philippine waters. The final pages contain treaty analysis, a cross-reference note, and a separate memorandum on territorial waters in the Rashin Maru case.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese salvage operations at the Kowa Maru wreck
subfiles.from: Jorge B. Vargas, Secretary to the President of the Philippines
subfiles.to: Administrative Assistant, Office of the U.S. High Commissioner, Manila
subfiles.about: Reports the movements and unauthorized salvage activity of Japanese boats and workers at the Kowa Maru wreck.
subfiles.summary: Vargas recounts the Kinsho Maru’s landing of four Japanese salvage workers near Balabac, the typhoon that destroyed the wreck, and the Rokkuko Maru No. 5’s unauthorized entry to collect them.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese salvage of the Kowa Maru
subfiles.from: Kiyoshi Uchiyama, Consul General for Japan
subfiles.to: Manuel L. Quezon, President of the Philippines
subfiles.about: Requests permission for Japanese vessels to break up and salvage the Kowa Maru.
subfiles.summary: Uchiyama conveys shipowner Kinsaburo Narumiya’s request to use Japanese salvage vessels, citing the lack of a suitable American or Philippine vessel.

subfiles.title: War Department forwarding letter on Kowa Maru salvage
subfiles.about: Forwards High Commissioner correspondence on Kowa Maru salvage.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the High Commissioner’s June 28 letter and attachments.

subfiles.title: Treaty Division note on reciprocal salvage rights
subfiles.from: Charles M. Barnes, Chief, Treaty Division
subfiles.about: Clarifies that proposed reciprocity language concerns salvage vessels operating in Japanese waters.
subfiles.summary: Barnes proposes wording focused on whether American or Philippine salvage vessels could operate reciprocally in Japanese territorial waters.

subfiles.title: War Department report of Philippine response
subfiles.about: Reports that the Philippine Commonwealth will follow State Department suggestions on salvage policy.
subfiles.summary: The High Commissioner says the Commonwealth government will be guided by State Department suggestions.

subfiles.title: War Department forwarding wreck correspondence and sketches
subfiles.about: Forwards the High Commissioner’s July 26 letter and two sketches of the Kowa Maru wreck.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a condition report and two copies of a wreck sketch.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner’s report on the condition of the Kowa Maru
subfiles.from: Wayne Coy, Office of the U.S. High Commissioner
subfiles.about: Relays E. M. Grimm’s inspection of the largely destroyed Kowa Maru wreck.
subfiles.summary: Grimm found the ship broken into pieces, more than half missing, and evidence that scrap metal had been cut away.

subfiles.title: Sketch of Kowa Maru wreck, first copy
subfiles.about: Shows the small remaining portion of the Kowa Maru near Balabac Light.
subfiles.summary: Sketch locates the wreck three miles off Balabac Light.

subfiles.title: Sketch of Kowa Maru wreck, second copy
subfiles.about: Duplicate annotated sketch of the Kowa Maru remains.
subfiles.summary: Marks the portion still present on the reef.

subfiles.title: War Department forwarding Philippine correspondence
subfiles.about: Forwards correspondence concerning the Philippine response to the Japanese salvage request.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the High Commissioner’s August 6 letter and Vargas’s March 25 reply.

subfiles.title: High Commissioner forwarding Vargas’s reply
subfiles.from: Wayne Coy, Office of the U.S. High Commissioner
subfiles.about: Sends Vargas’s response to the Japanese consul general.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a copy of the March 25 Philippine letter.

subfiles.title: Philippine refusal of immediate Kowa Maru salvage permission
subfiles.from: Jorge B. Vargas, Secretary to the President
subfiles.to: Kiyoshi Uchiyama, Consul General for Japan
subfiles.about: Declines the Japanese salvage request pending further State Department guidance.
subfiles.summary: Vargas finds no emergency after years of stranding and suggests pursuing the matter through diplomatic channels.

subfiles.title: Treaty Division analysis of foreign salvage vessels
subfiles.about: Reviews treaty and statutory provisions relevant to Japanese salvage vessels in Philippine waters.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum distinguishes ordinary treaty rules for wrecked cargo from permission for foreign salvage vessels to operate. It identifies limited reciprocal treaties with Britain and Mexico and finds no treaty permitting such operations in the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference note on shipwrecked Japanese nationals
subfiles.about: Points to another file on reciprocal treatment of shipwrecked Japanese nationals and vessels.
subfiles.summary: Notes advice to handle the issue through diplomatic channels.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the twelve-mile limit in the Rashin Maru case
subfiles.about: Explains the distinction between three-mile territorial waters and wider search or arrest authority.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum states that U.S. sovereignty extends three miles offshore, while certain searches or arrests may occur farther out under separate authority. It applies that distinction to a murder on a Japanese vessel ten miles off Hawaii.

subfiles.title: Illegible Far Eastern Affairs fragment
subfiles.about: Contains an unreadable fragment apparently concerning the twelve-mile limit.
subfiles.summary: Only a few words and the division heading are legible.
